reason: The hypothesis relies on premises about B2 phase formation and ductility improvement in RHEAs, but the cited evidence does not directly support these claims for the NbMoTaW system. E1 only states the general problem of RHEA brittleness, E2 discusses Hf effects in FCC HEAs and Ni-based superalloys, not BCC RHEAs, and E3 shows a BCC+B2 microstructure in a different alloy system (AlNbTaTiVZr) with limited ductility improvement (4.5% compression strain). No evidence supports the irradiation resistance premise.
premises: B2 precipitates can form in BCC refractory high-entropy alloys via heat treatment
A dual-phase BCC+B2 microstructure can improve room-temperature ductility in RHEAs
The continuous BCC matrix will maintain high-temperature strength
The BCC+B2 microstructure will not adversely affect irradiation resistance
Hf or similar alloying additions promote B2 phase formation and property enhancement
